title: Every point of the image of a smooth morphism admits an etale local section

standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma that smooth fibres over a field have dense closed points with finite separable residue fields (Varieties) and the slice lemma producing an etale locally closed slice through such a point (same chapter); cited inputs with the two-step argument written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Note X_s is nonempty since s lies in the image of f.
Apply the dense separable closed points lemma to obtain a closed point x of X_s with kappa(x)/kappa(s) finite separable.
Apply the slice lemma to get an immersion Z -> X with Z -> S etale and x in Z.
Conclude that (S', s') = (Z, x) is an etale neighbourhood of (S, s) with an S-morphism S' -> X.

proof_roadmap.step: Pick a closed point of the fibre with finite separable residue field via the density lemma.
Turn it into an etale slice through the slice lemma and take that slice as the etale neighbourhood.

difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism of schemes f : X -> S and a point s in the image, the lemma produces an etale neighbourhood (S', s') -> (S, s) together with an S-morphism S' -> X, i.e. smooth morphisms have etale local sections through image points. The retained first proof is complete: X_s is nonempty by assumption, the dense-separable-closed-points lemma (Varieties) yields a closed point x of X_s with kappa(x) finite separable over kappa(s), and the slice lemma then gives an immersion Z -> X with Z -> S etale and x in Z; taking (S', s') = (Z, x) is the conclusion. The statement block additionally carries the author's slogan and a reference environment citing EGA4, Corollaire 17.16.3 (ii). Retained author proof at lines 10859-10868.
